messages:
amy_sales: quick heads-up — ACME's POC is seeing a burst of 5xxs under sustained load (demo ramp). hitting this during a 200rps soak
julian_eng: thanks. can you paste the error pattern and timeframe?
maria_support: we got a stack of 502/504s and a few 503s starting ~11:12am UTC, persisted for ~3m then intermittently after. client saw timeouts too.
amy_sales: repro script they ran: 4 threads @50rps each, prompt sizes ~1.2k tokens. they also enabled client-side prefetch of cache entries to speed up repeated calls.
ashley_oncall: interesting — prefetching KV can amplify load on the Redis/cache layer and hold LRO slots. julian any idea if our frontdoor queue/backpressure thresholds are triggering?
julian_eng: looking at runtime traces now. seeing large spike in pending request queue depth and many requests hitting the model process with high kvcache-miss downstream calls. autoscaler scaled, but with ~35s lag — new workers came up after backlog hit 90th percentile latency.
kevin_sre: timeline: 
```
11:11:50 - client ramp start
11:12:20 - backend queue depth +420
11:12:45 - first 502s (model process OOM/timeout to redis)
11:13:30 - autoscale triggered (requested 3 more workers)
11:14:10 - workers registered
11:14:20 - partial recovery, intermittent 5xxs until 11:15
```

maria_support: logs show repeated timeouts to redis: "ERR timeout waiting for connection" and then model runtime returning 502 with message "upstream timeout".
julian_eng: root cause looks like synchronous prefetch load on the KV layer + insufficient connection pool sizing on the model side. prefetch made many parallel KV lookups per request and increased latency, which cascaded into request timeouts and autoscale lag made it worse.
amy_sales: customer claim: prefetch cut p99 latency in small tests but in larger soak it blew up. they want a quick mitigation to finish the POC demo in 30m.
ashley_oncall: mitigation options (fast):
- ask client to disable prefetch (client-side) — safest, immediate.
- throttle incoming concurrency via frontdoor rate-limit (we can set per-route burst=30, steady=100rps) — quick config change.
- if redis is the bottleneck, increase redis conn pool + enable pipelined prefetch (non-blocking) — requires ops change.
- temporarily pin them to a slightly smaller model variant that uses fewer KV hits per request.

julian_eng: for immediate demo I'd do: 1) tell client to disable prefetch, 2) enable a short per-route concurrency cap, 3) follow-up plan to tune kv pool and add async prefetch. I can push a rollback-friendly route cap now.
maria_support: I can message ACME to disable prefetch and flip the cap. amy want me to coordinate?
amy_sales: yes please, tell them to turn prefetch off and I'll call them. also confirm pricing impact — they asked if dedup/prefetch affects cost.
ultra_dummy: ops-bot: route-cap change request queued: change_id=chg-9953, target=acme-poc-route, cap=concurrency:30, burst:60
kevin_sre: applied cap, telemetry shows queue depth falling. monitoring alerts cleared after ~90s.
julian_eng: after cap applied, redis timeouts dropped to near zero and 5xxs stopped. we should still do post-mortem: add async prefetch pattern and autoscaler speed improvements for rapid spikes.
amy_sales: ACME on the line, turning off prefetch now — confirm when you see stable signals and we'll continue the demo.
maria_support: seeing stable success rate now, p50/p95 look good. passing to you for close.
amy_sales: thanks everyone — will debrief with ACME and log action items: 1) client disable prefetch for demo 2) SRE to size redis pool and pipeline prefetch 3) infra to investigate autoscale latency improvement 4) docs: warn about prefetch + high-concurrency soak.
julian_eng: adding action item: add an internal flag to detect synchronous prefetch patterns and auto-shed or recommend async model.
kevin_sre: filing followup ticket SRE-1249 for conn pool + SRE-1250 for autoscaler tune.
maria_support: closing loop with ACME, will update thread when they confirm post-demo. :white_check_mark:
